examples.signature: Use the contexts `The capital of France is` and `The capital of France was` to separate context from a probability distribution over next tokens
Construct a four-token toy vocabulary and compare two candidate next-token distributions rather than treating model output as one deterministic word
Sample repeatedly from the same toy next-token distribution to show why one model state can produce multiple continuations
Encode `unbelievable` with hypothetical whole-word, subword, and character tokenizers to compare discrete vocabulary choices and sequence lengths
Use a toy vocabulary mapping text pieces to integer IDs, then show that changing ID assignments without permuting model parameters breaks the tokenizer–model interface
Compare visible words, Unicode/byte representation, whitespace-sensitive pieces, special tokens, and token IDs to prevent collapsing distinct text representation layers
Convert next-token counts 3/1/1 into a normalized empirical distribution and verify nonnegative mass sums to one
Estimate `P(cat | the)` and `P(cat | a)` from separate context-conditioned count tables to show why conditioning changes the denominator
Compare predictive distributions with the same argmax but different concentration and separate next-token probability from whole-answer factual confidence
